Dear Learners,

Tomorrow is your English examination. Remember that you have already done a wonderful job preparing. Stay calm and use today for focused revision.

Revise Smartly

Review important class notes, worksheets, revision papers and suggested answers shared on Teams.
Revise the features and structure of each writing genre.
Quickly go through grammar, punctuation, vocabulary and literary devices.
Focus more on areas where you made mistakes during practice.
Do not try to complete every worksheet again tonight.

Tonight

Avoid trying to revise everything again.
Do a short and focused revision.
Organise everything you need for tomorrow.
Get enough rest and come to school with a fresh mind.

In the Exam Hall

Read the text and every question carefully.
Pay attention to key words in the question and the marks given.
Underline key ideas and use evidence from the text where needed.
Do not leave questions blank. If one takes too long, move on and return to it later.
Plan before writing and organise your ideas into clear paragraphs.
Proofread for grammar, spelling and punctuation.
Keep your answer script neat.

Believe in yourself. You have worked hard, practised well, and shown great improvement. Stay confident, read carefully, and give your best effort.

All the very best!

Sample Answer Key

Section A – Fill in the Blanks

1. copper

2. tin

3. bronze

4. metalworkers

5. artefacts

Section B – MCQ

1. b – It was harder and more durable.

2. a – Sickle

3. a – Graves and burials

4. a – Communities needed materials such as copper and tin.

5. a – They made bell-shaped pottery.

Section C – Short Answers

1. Copper was too soft for many strong tools and weapons.

2. Bronze tools were stronger and more durable, so land could be worked more efficiently and more food could be produced.

3. Any two: metalworkers, potters, traders, builders.

4. Any two: pottery can give clues about daily life, culture, trade or ceremonies.

Section D – Scenario-Based

1. The bronze sickle would be more useful because bronze was harder, sharper and more durable than copper.

2. Any two supported ideas: the person/society may have had burial customs or beliefs; skilled craftspeople; metalworking knowledge; wealth/status; trade links.

3. Extra food could support a larger population. It could also support specialist workers and trade, helping the settlement grow into a town or early city.

Section E – Critical Thinking

1. Communities needed copper and tin to make bronze. Because these materials were not available everywhere, people traded them between regions. This connected communities and also helped ideas and goods move.

2. Different evidence gives different clues. Tools may show technology and work, pottery may show daily life and trade, graves may show beliefs, and buildings may show organisation. Comparing evidence helps historians build a stronger explanation.

Section A – Fill in the Blanks

1. irrigation

2. pottery

Section B – MCQ

1. a – Oxen

2. a – Metals, pottery and jewellery

3. a – Craft skill, status, wealth and trade

4. a – Ships and travel

Section C – Short Answers

1. Bronze was made by mixing copper with tin. It was harder, sharper and more durable than copper.

2. Any two: animals provided milk, meat, butter or cheese; oxen helped plough land or pull carts.

3. Any two: settlement size, architecture, organisation or community life.

4. Any two: they were farmers; herders; skilled metalworkers; lived in small villages/family farms; traded and travelled; used metal tools and weapons.

Section D – Scenario-Based

1. They could trade copper and tin with each other. Both communities would gain materials they needed, helping them make bronze and strengthening trade links.

Marking:

1 mark – west of the Prime Meridian

2. Point Y – 30°S, 60°E [2]

Point Y is 30° south of the Equator and 60° east of the Prime Meridian.

Marking:

1 mark – south of the Equator
1 mark – east of the Prime Meridian

3. Point Z – 0°, 30°E [2]

Point Z is neither in the Northern nor Southern Hemisphere because it lies on the Equator (0° latitude).

Marking:

1 mark – neither Northern nor Southern Hemisphere / lies on the Equator
1 mark – explanation that 0° latitude is the Equator
F. Critical Thinking [3]

1. Two places are both at 30°N but have different longitudes. What is the same about their locations, and what is different?

Answer:
Both places are at 30°N latitude, so they are the same distance north of the Equator. They have different longitudes, so they are at different positions east or west of the Prime Meridian.
